messages:
sam: Taking over afternoon coverage — quick FYI on a few flaky signals I tracked this shift. I left short notes below, please add anything I missed. @marta you can swap in now :wave:

sam: Current noisy things: encoder-pool.high-latency (sporadic 95th spikes), kv-prefetch.rate-surge (short bursts around midnight UTC), and prefix-cache.false-positive (occasional alert flood when rollout jobs run).

marta: thx. where are you seeing the encoder spikes? dashboard link?

sam: Encoder spikes are visible on /dash/encoder/latency, focused to nodegroup "enc-rt-eu-2". Most correlate with long sequence generation (>1024). Simple prom query:```sum(rate(encoder_request_duration_seconds_bucket{le="0.5"}[5m])) by (nodegroup)``` but look at p95/p99 as well.

anika: FYI the rollout job that caused prefix-cache alerts ran at 15:20; I muted that rule for 20m while it blew up. Mute in #alerts: `rule:prefix-cache.false-positive` — will add to runbook.

ryan: I added a short note in runbook/coverage.md — suggest we make the alert condition require sustained rate > 10/min for 3m to reduce noise.

sam: Good call. For kv-prefetch, it's noisy on the eu-west pools when bursty traffic hits cold models. Short-term mitigation: raise threshold for the preftech alert and add annotation to ignore if `server:bursting=true`.

marta: swapping in now. Sam — anything I need to ack or take ownership of?

sam: If you see encoder p95 > 250ms on enc-rt-eu-2 for >2mins, escalate to infra oncall (pager infra-team). Otherwise just monitor charts and unmute alerts if things persist. Also watch for increased OOMs in encoder pods — seen 2x in last 24h.

oncall-bot: Reminder: scheduled canary deployment at 18:30 UTC for model-runner-v2. If that goes noisy, do automatic rollback per policy.

marta: got it. I'll keep the canary in mind. tagging @ryan to follow up with a PR for the alert tweak.

ryan: will submit PR in ~30m. Also adding a quick diagnostic snippet you can paste in shell to dump recent 5m encoder tails:```for pod in $(kubectl get pods -l app=encoder -o name); do kubectl logs $pod --since=5m | tail -n 50; done```

anika: note: I observed a pattern where the preftech spikes align with a specific customer workload (customer-id: c-219). I left a note in the customer-ops ticket so support can correlate.

sam: awesome — thanks team. Leaving a couple of flags in the handoff: (1) encoder p95 trend, (2) kv-prefetch bursts (watch c-219), (3) prefix-cache false alert rule. I'll be reachable on DMs if anything flares up. :thumbsup:

marta: taking it from here. will ping if anything deviates. swapping ETA 20:10 UTC. :eyes:
